title: Data Types
description: The kinds of values in Python: numbers, text, and yes/no answers.

content.value: Every value has a **data type**: what kind of thing it is. The type decides what you can do with it. Click any chip to see what Python calls each value.

items.title: int (integer)
items.text: Whole numbers. Use them for counting things.

items.title: float
items.text: Numbers with a decimal point. The name comes from "floating point".

content.caption: The dot is what makes a number a float.

content.value:
apples = 5      # int
cookies = 2.5   # float
height = 4.2    # float
print(apples)
print(cookies)

content.question: What type is `3.0`?
content.explain: It has a decimal point, so it is a `float`, even though the part after the dot is zero.

items: A **string** (`str`) is text: letters, words, whole sentences.
Wrap it in quotes. Double `" "` or single `' '` both work.
Start and end with the same kind of quote.

parts.label: start
parts.note: The opening quote tells Python: text starts here.

parts.label: the text
parts.note: Everything between the quotes is kept exactly as written, spaces and all.

parts.label: end
parts.note: The closing quote must match the opening one.

content.value:
hero_name = "Batman"
secret_message = 'I love coding!'
print(hero_name)
print(secret_message)

items.title: 7 is an int
items.text: A number. Adding works: the result is `10`.

items.title: "7" is a str
items.text: Text, because of the quotes. Python cannot add text to a number, so it stops with a `TypeError`.

content.question: What type is `"42"`?
content.explain: The quotes make it text. It looks like a number, but Python treats it as a `str`.

content.text: A switch is either on or off, never in between. A boolean is either `True` or `False`, nothing else.

items: They answer yes or no questions: Is the game over? Is the door open?
Capital first letter, and no quotes.

content.value:
game_over = False
logged_in = True
print(game_over)
print(logged_in)

items.title: Breaks
items.text: Lowercase `true` is an error. `"True"` with quotes is just text, not a boolean.

content.question: Which line stores a boolean?
content.explain: `True` with a capital T and no quotes is a boolean. With quotes it becomes a string.

editorCode:
apples = 5
cookies = 2.5
hero = "Spiderman"
game_over = False

print(apples)
print(cookies)
print(hero)
print(game_over)

practice.question: Make a string variable called 'pet_name' with the name of a pet, then print it.
Make a boolean called 'is_sunny' and set it to True. Print it.

quiz.question: Which of these is a float?
quiz.explain: A float is a number with a decimal point, like 3.14. `10` is a whole number (integer) and "Hello" is text (a string).

quiz.question: What is wrong with this line: name = Batman
options: Batman is not a real name.
quiz.explain: Text must be wrapped in quotation marks. Without them, Python thinks `Batman` is a variable name and gives an error.

quiz.question: What type is the value `"7"` (with quotes)?
quiz.explain: The quotation marks make it text (a string). Without the quotes, `7` would be an int.
